articles.title: 2026 iCARDIO Alliance Global Implementation Guidelines on Heart Failure.
articles.dek: The 2026 iCARDIO Alliance Global Implementation Guidelines provide updated evidence-based recommendations for heart failure management tailored to diverse healthcare settings and resource constraints worldwide.
summary: This is an updated 2026 version of international implementation guidelines for heart failure management developed by the iCARDIO Alliance. The guidelines address heart failure across multiple phenotypes: acute and chronic heart failure, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), heart failure with improved ejection fraction, and cardiomyopathies. The document aims to reconcile inconsistencies in global healthcare access, infrastructure variability, resource limitations, and diverse local clinical practices.

The guidelines integrate current evidence with novel therapies while providing context-specific recommendations tailored to individual patient needs. A distinctive feature is the inclusion of 'economic adjustment' recommendations designed for settings with 'somewhat limited' or 'severely limited' resources. The document encompasses pharmacological, non-pharmacological, invasive, and interventional management strategies, with emphasis on improving patient outcomes and reducing hospitalization burden.

These guidelines represent group consensus incorporating existing published guidelines while adding new recommendations where recent evidence has emerged. The authors acknowledge the need for universal recommendations that address unique challenges faced by patients and providers globally, presenting a unified strategy applicable across varying healthcare contexts and resource availability.
articles.why: Global heart failure guidelines that acknowledge resource constraints may help clinicians in diverse settings adapt evidence-based care to local contexts. The inclusion of 'economic adjustment' pathways could inform discussions about feasible care delivery in low- and middle-income regions, though implementation effectiveness and outcome impacts in resource-limited settings are not specified in this abstract.
articles.evidence: This is a clinical practice guideline document representing expert consensus. The abstract does not report a study design with sample sizes, patient populations, or outcome data. No trial registration, specific efficacy measures, or comparative effectiveness data are provided. Major limitations include the absence of empirical results, effectiveness data for resource-limited contexts, or evidence grading details for individual recommendations. The full document's strength-of-evidence assessments and data synthesis methods are not described in this abstract.

articles.title: Real-world evaluation of 2023-2024 XBB.1.5 mRNA and protein-based COVID-19 vaccine reactogenicity from the randomized BEEHIVE trial.
articles.dek: A randomized controlled trial found that the 2023-2024 Novavax protein-based COVID-19 vaccine produced fewer reported side effects than the Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA vaccine in people with prior mRNA vaccination.
summary: The BEEHIVE trial (NCT06065176) was a double-blinded, randomized, controlled study comparing reactogenicity between two 2023-2024 XBB.1.5 COVID-19 vaccines. Participants (n=901 vaccinated: 448 Novavax, 453 Pfizer-BioNTech) had previously received ≥2 doses of mRNA-based vaccine. Participants received one dose of either vaccine or served as an unvaccinated comparator group. Solicited side effects were tracked via electronic survey on days 1, 2, and 6 post-vaccination.

On day 1, significantly lower proportions in the Novavax group reported systemic events (62.1% vs. 75.7%, risk difference −13.7%) or local injection-site events (81.0% vs. 92.7%, risk difference −11.7%) compared to Pfizer-BioNTech (both P<0.0001). The mean number of events per person was significantly lower for Novavax on days 1 and 2 (P<0.0001 each). Most reported events were mild, and reactogenicity declined throughout the week, with >80% reporting no systemic events and >94% reporting no local events by day 6 in both groups.

These findings demonstrate a measurable difference in reported reactogenicity profiles between the two vaccine platforms in this randomized comparison. The clinical significance of these differences—which were primarily in frequency rather than severity—and their relevance to individual vaccination decisions requires additional clinical context.
articles.why: Real-world comparison data on reactogenicity between vaccine platforms may inform discussions about vaccine selection, particularly for individuals with prior adverse reactions to mRNA vaccines or concerns about side effects. Understanding that differences exist and their magnitude may help clinicians counsel patients, though the mild nature of most events and the rapid resolution by day 6 should be considered in context.

evidence.design: Double-blinded, randomized, controlled trial with 1:1 randomization to Novavax or Pfizer-BioNTech, plus a non-vaccinated comparator group
evidence.population: Adults with prior receipt of ≥2 doses of mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccine
evidence.outcomes: Solicited systemic (fatigue, fever, headache, joint pain, malaise, muscle pain, nausea/vomiting) and local (injection-site pain, tenderness, swelling) reactogenicity on days 1, 2, and 6
limitations_and_uncertainties: Abstract does not provide demographic details (age, sex, comorbidities) or baseline characteristics of the groups
No information on severity grading criteria or definition of 'mild' vs. more severe events
No data on severe adverse events or hospitalizations
Abstract does not report findings from the non-vaccinated comparator group
No mention of follow-up duration beyond day 6
Electronic survey methodology may be subject to recall or reporting bias
The clinical significance of the observed differences is not discussed in the abstract

articles.title: Child Maltreatment During COVID-19: Triangulating Data Across Reporting Sources.
articles.dek: A systematic review found conflicting patterns in child maltreatment reporting during COVID-19, with child welfare data showing declines but self-report studies showing increases.
summary: This systematic review examined scientific literature on child maltreatment rates during the COVID-19 pandemic using PRISMA criteria. The authors identified 4,193 unique studies and included 73 that met eligibility criteria. They triangulated data across three sources: child welfare administrative records, hospital reports, and self-report studies to assess whether known pandemic stressors (economic hardship, social isolation, school closures) corresponded with changes in child abuse and neglect.

Results differed substantially by data source. Child welfare sources documented declining child maltreatment reports immediately after COVID-19 onset. In contrast, self-report studies documented an increasing trend in maltreatment. Hospital data findings were largely mixed, with more studies reporting decreased child maltreatment during COVID-19 than increased rates.

The authors conclude that interpreting child maltreatment surveillance data from the COVID-19 period requires careful consideration of evidence from multiple reporting sources, as conclusions about trends can differ substantially depending on which data source predominates in the analysis.
articles.why: This review highlights an important methodological consideration in child maltreatment surveillance: different reporting systems (administrative, clinical, self-report) may yield conflicting signals about true prevalence changes. The discrepancy between declining administrative reports and increasing self-report data may reflect reduced opportunities for detection (school closures, less clinical contact) rather than actual changes in maltreatment. Understanding these data source limitations is relevant for policymakers and child protective services in interpreting surveillance trends and informing resource allocation during public health crises.

evidence.design: Systematic review using PRISMA criteria; reviewed observational data from administrative sources, hospital records, and self-report studies
evidence.sample_size: 73 studies met eligibility criteria from 4,193 unique studies identified
evidence.major_limitations: Abstract does not specify: inclusion/exclusion criteria applied, date range of literature searched, geographic scope of included studies, heterogeneity of outcome definitions across studies, quality assessment methods, or effect sizes by data source. Cannot determine from abstract whether meta-analysis was conducted. Results depend heavily on which studies were included and how maltreatment was operationalized across different sources.
evidence.uncertainty: High uncertainty regarding true direction and magnitude of maltreatment changes; directionality differs by reporting source. The full text would clarify whether differences reflect true epidemiologic changes, detection bias, or differences in reporting practices across systems.

articles.title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.
articles.dek: A Canadian clinical practice update provides evidence-based guidance for patient evaluation and management in transcatheter mitral and tricuspid valve intervention.
summary: This is a clinical practice update from the Canadian Cardiovascular Society, Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery, and Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology addressing the evaluation and management of patients with severe, symptomatic mitral or tricuspid valve regurgitation. The update synthesizes contemporary evidence on transcatheter valve interventions, including edge-to-edge repair and valve replacement as less invasive alternatives to surgical intervention.

The update emphasizes key evaluation domains: clinical presentation of valve lesions, diagnostic assessment using multimodality imaging and hemodynamic evaluation, patient selection criteria, and procedural and long-term outcomes. A central recommendation is timely referral and structured multidisciplinary assessment to identify appropriate candidates for intervention.

The authors conclude that transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or replacement can provide symptomatic relief and improved quality of life in carefully selected patients when conducted within a collaborative multidisciplinary heart team model that includes cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists, heart failure specialists, and nursing partners. The document emphasizes that optimal outcomes require active engagement from referring physicians and comprehensive post-intervention follow-up.
articles.why: This update is relevant for clinicians managing patients with severe mitral or tricuspid regurgitation who may benefit from transcatheter rather than surgical approaches. The guidance may help inform referral decision-making and patient counseling regarding available treatment options, particularly regarding the importance of multidisciplinary evaluation and the potential for symptom improvement. The emphasis on timely referral suggests value in maintaining clinical awareness of appropriate candidates for these interventions.
articles.evidence: This is a clinical practice update, not a primary research study. The abstract does not specify a trial design, sample size, or primary data collection. The update synthesizes existing evidence and clinical experience; specific numerical outcomes, effect sizes, and confidence intervals are not reported in the abstract. Major limitations include the absence of detailed information about the evidence synthesis methodology, the specific studies reviewed, and the strength of evidence for individual recommendations. The abstract does not provide sufficient detail to assess the comprehensiveness of the evidence base or the certainty of conclusions.

articles.title: [Chinese expert consensus on the clinical application of lung biopsy in interstitial lung disease].
articles.dek: Chinese expert consensus provides standardized, evidence-based recommendations for lung biopsy decision-making and management across the full clinical pathway in interstitial lung disease.
summary: This is a multidisciplinary expert consensus statement developed by the Respiratory Physicians Branch of the Chinese Medical Doctor Association and the Chinese Thoracic Society, incorporating expertise from respiratory medicine, radiology, pathology, thoracic surgery, and rheumatology. The consensus was formulated using systematic literature review, evidence grading, and the Delphi method for anonymous expert voting. It culminates in 15 recommendations addressing the complete biopsy management pathway.

The recommendations address key decision points: (1) need for multidisciplinary discussion (MDD) before biopsy; (2) biopsy indications stratified by high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) patterns (definite UIP pattern generally discourages biopsy; indeterminate or non-UIP patterns with insufficient clinical evidence strongly recommend it); (3) selection among four biopsy techniques based on clinical context (transbronchial lung biopsy for suspected granulomatous disease; transbronchial cryobiopsy as preferred modality in expert centers; surgical lung biopsy for fibrotic patterns; percutaneous transthoracic needle biopsy for nodular lesions); (4) shared decision-making throughout; and (5) post-biopsy MDD for integrated diagnosis.

The consensus emphasizes systematic perioperative management to prevent acute exacerbation of ILD, standardized histopathological reporting using international nomenclature, and careful specimen collection from multiple sites including disease-normal interfaces. Biopsy is contraindicated in acute respiratory failure, severe functional impairment, hemodynamic instability, and end-stage debilitation. The framework addresses special clinical contexts including ILD complicated by lung cancer or connective tissue disease.
articles.why: This consensus provides structured guidance for clinicians managing diagnostic uncertainty in ILD, a heterogeneous group of disorders where histopathology can substantially alter diagnosis and treatment. The recommendation to tailor biopsy decisions based on HRCT patterns and integrate results through structured MDD may help standardize practice, reduce unnecessary procedures, and improve diagnostic accuracy. The emphasis on shared decision-making and perioperative safety addresses practical implementation challenges.
articles.evidence: This is a consensus statement, not original research. It synthesizes evidence through systematic literature review and expert input using the Delphi method. Individual recommendations carry varying evidence levels (ranging from Level 1 to Level 4, with Level 1 typically representing highest-quality evidence). No patient cohort, sample size, or primary data are reported. The strength and applicability of recommendations depend on the underlying evidence base, which is not detailed in the abstract. Limitations include that consensus represents expert opinion at a particular time and may require updating as evidence evolves; applicability to healthcare systems outside China may vary.

articles.title: Entrustable professional activities in medical education: strategies and results - a systematic review.
articles.dek: A systematic review of 478 published studies identified diverse strategies for developing, implementing, and assessing Entrustable Professional Activities in medical education, with most research focused on postgraduate training in the USA.
summary: This systematic review searched six electronic databases (updated through March 2025) to characterize evidence on Entrustable Professional Activities (EPAs)—a framework designed to address challenges in Competence-Based Medical Education. Reviewers extracted data from 478 studies and assessed quality using the Quality Assessment Tool for Studies with Diverse Designs (QATSDD). The majority of included studies (59.6%) examined postgraduate medical education, and over half (51.5%) were conducted in the USA.

The review found substantial methodological diversity across studies in how EPAs were developed, implemented, and assessed. Over half of studies (50.8%) addressed factors influencing EPA implementation, and 46.4% discussed how EPAs might improve learning and assessment practices. However, few studies examined cost-effectiveness of EPA use. Overall, quality assessment revealed modest results across the included studies.

The authors conclude that while EPA adoption is increasing across diverse educational contexts and settings, significant challenges remain—particularly regarding the quality of available evidence. The review highlights the need for further high-quality research to strengthen the evidence base and clarify implementation strategies.
articles.why: EPAs represent an evolving approach within medical education to make competency assessment more practical and observable. Understanding the diversity of implementation strategies and their effects may help educators and program directors design EPA frameworks appropriate to their institutional contexts. The modest quality of existing evidence suggests that educators should interpret current EPA literature cautiously when planning local implementations.

evidence.design: Systematic review of published studies using electronic database searches
evidence.sample_size: 478 studies included for data extraction and analysis
evidence.limitations_and_uncertainty: The abstract does not report inter-rater reliability, protocol registration, or details on publication bias assessment. The modest quality findings across included studies limit the strength of conclusions. The review does not provide specific effect sizes, randomized trial data, or comparative outcome measures. No individual patient-level data were analyzed. The review characterizes the state of the evidence rather than establishing causality.

articles.tag: ANKYLOSING SPONDYLITIS / SHOCK WAVE THERAPY / REHABILITATION
articles.title: Focused Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy Versus Therapeutic Ultrasound as Adjuncts to Exercise-Based Rehabilitation for Functional Limitation in Ankylosing Spondylitis: An Assessor-Blinded Randomized Comparative Trial.
articles.dek: In ankylosing spondylitis patients receiving exercise-based rehabilitation, focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy was associated with greater improvements in functional capacity and disability at 12 months compared with therapeutic ultrasound.
summary: This assessor-blinded randomized comparative trial enrolled 106 ankylosing spondylitis patients with chronic lumbar stiffness (90 completed 12-month follow-up). Participants received either weekly focused extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) for 4 weeks (n=45) or therapeutic ultrasound 3 times weekly for 4 weeks (n=45), with both groups receiving identical 12-week supervised exercise and stable pharmacotherapy. The primary outcome was functional capacity measured by the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index (BASFI); secondary outcomes included disease activity (BASDAI), pain, spinal mobility, and disability (DFI).

Both groups showed significant improvements across all measured outcomes at 12 months. The ESWT group demonstrated lower BASFI scores (2.2±1.8 vs. 3.7±2.3; p=0.001) and lower disability scores (p=0.003) compared with the ultrasound group. Lumbar mobility differed nominally between groups (p=0.030) but did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. No significant between-group differences were observed for disease activity (p=0.424) or pain (p=0.284).

The authors conclude that focused ESWT showed greater long-term functional improvement than therapeutic ultrasound when added to identical exercise and pharmacotherapy. However, they emphasize that without an exercise-only control arm, the incremental benefit of either modality over exercise alone cannot be determined, and findings should be interpreted as exploratory given lack of prospective registration and other methodological limitations.
articles.why: This trial addresses an evidence gap in comparative effectiveness of adjunctive physical modalities for ankylosing spondylitis. The findings suggest potential differential effects between ESWT and ultrasound on functional outcomes, which could inform clinical discussions about treatment sequencing and modality selection. However, the inability to isolate the contribution of either modality over exercise alone limits clinical interpretation. Results may be useful for practitioners discussing options with patients but require confirmation before shifting clinical practice.
articles.evidence: Assessor-blinded randomized comparative trial with 106 enrolled participants and 90 completers (85% retention). Major limitations include: lack of prospective trial registration, absence of an exercise-only control arm (preventing determination of incremental benefit over exercise), unequal treatment frequencies between groups (ESWT weekly vs. ultrasound 3×/week), and acknowledged exploratory rather than definitive status. Secondary outcomes did not survive multiple comparison correction. No confidence intervals reported. Publication date and trial conduct timeframe (March 2024–August 2025) provided but full methodological detail unavailable from abstract.

articles.title: Concordance of Microbiological and Histopathological Examination of Bone Biopsies in Diagnosing Diabetic Foot Osteomyelitis, a Systematic Review.
articles.dek: A systematic review finds modest concordance between histopathology and microbiology results in bone biopsies for diabetic foot osteomyelitis, with each method offering distinct diagnostic strengths.
summary: This systematic review examined five studies totaling 308 patients with diabetic foot osteomyelitis (DFO) who underwent bone biopsy with both histopathological and microbiological testing. The review synthesized evidence on diagnostic concordance, test performance characteristics, and clinical outcomes associated with each method.

Histopathology and microbiology showed modest concordance, with a mean concordant positive rate of 43.4%. Histopathology demonstrated higher specificity, while microbiology had higher sensitivity (70–83.9%) but was more susceptible to contamination. Positive histopathology was more strongly associated with need for revision surgery or extended antibiotic therapy.

The authors concluded that histopathology offers superior diagnostic specificity while microbiology provides valuable information for antimicrobial stewardship. The frequent discordance between methods suggests results should be interpreted within the broader clinical context rather than in isolation.
articles.why: Diabetic foot osteomyelitis is a serious complication with high morbidity and amputation risk. This review addresses uncertainty about the optimal diagnostic approach when bone biopsy is performed, highlighting that neither test alone captures complete diagnostic information. The differential utility of each method—specificity for histology versus sensitivity and organism identification for microbiology—may inform how clinicians weigh results when they diverge, and supports individualized interpretation based on clinical presentation.
articles.evidence: Systematic review of five studies (n = 308 patients total) using quantitative narrative synthesis. Major limitations include small number of included studies, heterogeneity in study design and definitions (acknowledged as requiring standardization), lack of information on individual study quality assessment methods, and inability to perform meta-analysis. The abstract does not specify whether studies were prospective or retrospective. Sensitivity ranges are wide (70–83.9%), suggesting variability across studies. No confidence intervals or statistical testing results are reported.

articles.title: Age and antiplatelet de-escalation after myocardial infarction in the TALOS-AMI trial.
articles.dek: In stabilized patients one month after heart attack treatment with stent placement, switching from ticagrelor to clopidogrel reduced adverse events and bleeding in those under 75 years old, but benefits were uncertain in older adults.
summary: TALOS-AMI was a randomized trial of 2,697 participants (mean age 60 years, 16.8% women) who were event-free one month after percutaneous coronary intervention for acute myocardial infarction. Patients receiving aspirin and ticagrelor were randomly assigned to either de-escalate to aspirin and clopidogrel or continue the original therapy, with follow-up through one year.

Among patients younger than 75 years (n=2,376), de-escalation reduced the composite primary endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events or serious bleeding from 7.2% to 4.1%, and reduced bleeding alone from 4.9% to 2.8%. Among patients 75 years and older, the primary endpoint occurred in 11.6% of the continuation group versus 6.4% of the de-escalation group, and bleeding in 7.9% versus 3.2%, but these differences were not statistically significant. No significant age-treatment interaction was detected for any measured outcome.

The results suggest de-escalation from ticagrelor to clopidogrel may benefit younger, stabilized post-infarction patients, but uncertainty remains about safety and efficacy in adults aged 75 and older due to the smaller sample size and wider confidence intervals in that subgroup. The authors note that most bleeding events in older patients occurred within the first six months.
articles.why: This analysis addresses a clinically important question about whether antiplatelet therapy recommendations should differ by age in post-myocardial infarction patients. The finding of potential benefit in younger patients while showing uncertain effects in older adults could inform individualized treatment discussions, particularly given the increased bleeding risk in elderly patients. The lack of a significant age-treatment interaction statistically does not exclude clinically meaningful differences in the older population due to sample size limitations.
articles.evidence: Randomized controlled trial with prespecified secondary analysis stratified by age. Sample: 2,697 participants (2,376 aged <75 years; 321 aged ≥75 years). Major limitations include the substantially smaller sample of older adults, resulting in wider confidence intervals that cross the null for the ≥75 group; inability to determine whether de-escalation is truly equivalent or simply underpowered in older patients; and lack of information about adherence or reasons for treatment discontinuation. The abstract does not provide details about baseline comorbidities, kidney function, or other factors relevant to older adults.
